title: Slack apps with Bolt
bridge: A Bolt app is like an Express app for Slack: app.command, app.action and app.event are routes with handlers. Except: in Socket Mode Slack never calls a URL of ours; our app dials out over a WebSocket. And every request must be acknowledged within 3 seconds, or the person sees an error.
intro: People hand work to Nova and follow it in Slack, where they already talk. This lesson builds the pieces of our Slack app. A slash command, one status message per ticket, buttons that become signals, and replies that become answers. Every click records who made it.

picture.caption: A click travels over our app's own WebSocket to a Temporal signal. Then the message is edited so the button cannot fire twice.

steps.text: at start, opens a WebSocket to Slack with the app token; no public URL
sends the click over the socket; the handler calls ack() at once
maps the Slack user ID to a person: email, Jira accountId, GitHub login
signals decidePlan with who decided and the plan version

sections.h: Socket Mode: our app dials out
p: A normal Slack app gives Slack a public URL, and Slack sends every command and click there. Socket Mode turns this around. Our app opens a WebSocket to Slack, and Slack sends events down that socket. We publish no endpoint, so there is nothing to attack from outside.

Two tokens do this. The app-level token starts with xapp- and has the connections:write scope; it opens the socket. The bot token starts with xoxb-; it calls Slack's Web API, such as chat.postMessage. Both come from Vault infrastructure/ai-agents/slack-app through an ExternalSecret.

callout.text: G3-30: Socket Mode means no public endpoint. Like the Jira poll, it keeps every connection outbound.

p: app.command("/nova", handler) runs the handler when someone types /nova. The handler gets ack, the command (text, user_id, channel_id) and respond. Slack waits at most 3 seconds for ack(). If it does not come, the person sees an error such as operation_timeout, even if your code finishes later.
So call ack() first, then do the slow work: Temporal, Jira, Slack calls. respond() sends a reply only the person who typed the command can see, an ephemeral message.
sections.because: We ack before calling Temporal because a slow Temporal call must never turn into an error in front of the person.

notes.text: Three options make Socket Mode: the bot token, the app token and socketMode: true.
ack() first, always. Everything after it may take as long as it needs.
One word means start: /nova RH-1234. Two words: a verb and a key.
JIRA_KEY is a regex like /^RH-\d+$/, defined in the shared package.
respond() answers the person privately; nobody else in the channel sees usage help.
start() connects the socket. The process then waits for events.

p: Each verb is one Temporal call by workflow ID. start goes through startRun, so /nova and the Jira poll join the same run. status is the run's status query. stop is the stop signal, carrying the person who asked.

G4-05 later changes start: /nova sets the issue property nova.requester and assigns the ticket to Nova, and the poll does the rest. Then a ticket handed over in Slack is recorded in Jira the same way as one assigned in Jira.
sections.because: We map every verb to a start, a query or a signal because a run's state lives only in the workflow.

notes.text: Who typed it, looked up in config/people.yaml. Every action records a person.
A handle by ID; nova:RH-1234 is the ticket's run.
The same startRun as the poll: same ID, same queue, USE_EXISTING.
A query answers from the run's state. oneLine turns it into one readable line.
The stop signal carries by, so Jira and the PR show who stopped the run.

sections.h: One status message, edited in place
p: Each ticket gets one thread in the Nova channel. Its first message is the status: Checking, Planning, Awaiting approval, Working, PR open, or Needs info and Stopped. chat.postMessage returns the message's channel and ts. ts is the message's ID, a timestamp string like 1760364000.123456.

With channel and ts we edit that message with chat.update at every state change, instead of posting a new one. A reply inside the thread is chat.postMessage with thread_ts set to the first message's ts. The broker stores channel and ts as the run's Slack scope, so the run may post only there.
sections.because: We edit one message instead of posting many because people should see the state at a glance, without noise.

notes.text: The first message of the thread. text is required; it is also what notifications show.
channel and ts identify the message from now on. Keep them in workflow state.
chat.update needs the same channel and ts. Only the bot that posted it may edit it.
thread_ts makes this a reply in the thread, not a new top-level message.

p: Buttons are Block Kit: Slack's JSON format for message layout. A button has an action_id (what it does) and a value (our data). G4-14 puts the workflow ID and plan version in the value: nova:RH-1234|v2. An old button for v1 can then never approve v2.

app.action matches action_ids. The handler acks, checks who clicked, sends the signal, and edits the message so the buttons are gone. If Temporal is down, the person is told to try again; a decision is never dropped silently.

The Change button opens a modal instead: a pop-up form inside Slack. client.views.open({ trigger_id, view }) opens it. The trigger_id comes with the click and is valid for only 3 seconds, so ack first and open the modal right away.

The view is Block Kit JSON with a callback_id and input blocks. When the person presses Submit, Slack sends a view_submission event. app.view(callback_id, handler) receives it, acks, and reads the typed text from view.state.values. Walkthrough g3-13 sends that text to the run as a change decision.
sections.because: We remove the buttons after a decision because an old button must not fire twice; the workflow also ignores a late decision.

notes.text: One table from action_id to signal name. plan_change opens a modal instead.
Narrow the types: this handler only serves button clicks in messages.
The value split: workflow ID and plan version.
Only the requester decides a plan. Anyone else gets an ephemeral refusal.
Change asks for free text in a modal; its submit handler sends decidePlan with the comment.
The signal, by workflow ID. The payload names who decided.
Temporal unreachable: say so to the person. Never swallow a decision.
Edit the clicked message: who decided, no buttons.

p: Slack knows a person by a member ID like U0123ABCD. Jira knows them by an accountId, GitHub by a login. config/people.yaml maps the three for about 25 people, and Sean keeps it. The tickets define the fields, not the exact layout, so treat this block as a sketch.
Every signal carries the person, so the run can write who approved in Jira and the PR. The GitHub login becomes the PR's Requested-by line (p9-3).
sections.because: We keep one mapping file because three tools name each person differently, and every wall depends on who is who.

code.text:
# ai-agents/config/people.yaml (people block, sketch): one entry per person, kept by Sean (G4-05)
people:
  - name: Dana Levi
    email: dana@example.com
    slack: U0123ABCD           # Slack member ID (profile, three dots, Copy member ID)
    jira: "712020:4c1d0e..."   # Jira accountId
    github: dana-l             # GitHub login: written on the PR as Requested-by: @dana-l
# teams: and owners: blocks follow (G5-07)

notes.text: The Slack member ID: what Bolt gives you as user_id or body.user.id.
The Jira accountId: what the changelog and the assignee field use (p9-2).
The GitHub login: the requester who may never approve this agent's PR.
The same file holds the teams and owners blocks from G5-07.

sections.h: Replies in a thread are answers
p: When Nova asks a question, a person answers by replying in the ticket's thread. app.event("message") receives every message in channels the bot is in. We keep only messages from people, inside a thread, in a thread that belongs to a run.
That needs the message.channels event and the channels:history scope. The broker recorded which workflow posted in which thread, so the app can find the run.
sections.because: We filter out bot messages and subtypes because Nova's own posts must never count as answers.

notes.text: subtype covers edits and joins; bot_id covers bots, Nova included; no thread_ts means not a reply.
Which run owns this thread? The broker stored it when the run posted.
answerQuestion with the text and who wrote it. The workflow joins several replies.

lab.title: A button that approves a Temporal run
youNeed: A free Slack workspace of your own (slack.com, Create a new workspace)
~/temporal-lab with the dev server and worker running (hello waits for approve)

worked.do:
In your workspace create a channel #nova-lab. Go to api.slack.com/apps and click Create New App, then From a manifest. Pick your workspace, choose YAML and paste:
display_information:
  name: nova-lab
features:
  bot_user:
    display_name: nova-lab
  slash_commands:
    - command: /nova-lab
      description: Start a lab run
      usage_hint: RH-1
oauth_config:
  scopes:
    bot: [commands, chat:write, channels:history]
settings:
  event_subscriptions:
    bot_events: [message.channels]
  interactivity:
    is_enabled: true
  socket_mode_enabled: true

Basic Information, App-Level Tokens, Generate: name socket, scope connections:write. Copy the xapp- token. Then Install to Workspace and copy the Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-) from OAuth & Permissions.
worked.see: Two tokens, one starting xapp-, one xoxb-

worked.do: In a terminal: export SLACK_APP_TOKEN=<the xapp- token> SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=<the xoxb- token>. Never commit them; they are only for your test workspace.

worked.see: nova-lab is running in Socket Mode
A message from nova-lab: *RH-1*: waiting for approval, with a green Approve button

worked.do: temporal workflow query --namespace ai-agents --workflow-id lab:RH-1 --name status

worked.see: The message changes to 'lab:RH-1: approved by @you' and the button is gone

lab.faded: Add a status verb: /nova-lab status RH-2 answers with respond() and the run's status query, visible only to you. Left to you: splitting command.text into verb and key, and the query call.
lab.alone: Make thread replies work. A reply in the waiting message's thread sends the approve signal, with the reply's text as the approver. Use app.event("message") with the filter from the lesson. Find the run in a Map from message ts to workflow ID, filled when you post.
lab.done: A slash command started a run and a button click signalled it. The message was edited so the button could not be clicked twice.

quiz.q: Your /nova handler calls Temporal first and ack() after. Temporal takes 4 seconds. What does the person see?

options.text: An error such as operation_timeout, even though the run started
options.why: Slack gives up after 3 seconds without ack(); ack first, then work.

options.text: Nothing unusual; Bolt acks for you
options.why: Bolt does not ack for you; you call ack() yourself.

options.text: A second copy of the command, retried by Slack
options.why: Slack reports the timeout to the person; it does not rerun the command for you.

quiz.q: Why does the plan button's value carry "nova:RH-1234|v2"?

options.text: Because Slack requires a version number in every button
options.why: value is free text for our own use.

options.text: So the handler finds the run, and an old v1 button can never approve plan v2
options.why: Workflow ID plus plan version: the right run, the right plan.

options.text: So the Slack app can work without config/people.yaml
options.why: The value says which run; people.yaml says who clicked.

quiz.q: Which message should the thread handler turn into answerQuestion?

options.text: Nova's own progress post in the thread
options.why: bot_id filters out Nova's posts; they are never answers.

options.text: A new top-level message in the Nova channel
options.why: No thread_ts: it belongs to no run's question.

options.text: A person's reply inside a ticket's thread
options.why: People only, inside a thread that a run owns.

words.plain: Our Slack app opens a WebSocket to Slack, so Slack never needs a public URL of ours.
The xapp- token with connections:write that opens the Socket Mode connection.
The xoxb- token the app uses to call Slack's Web API, such as chat.postMessage.
Tells Slack the request arrived; must be called within 3 seconds.
Slack's JSON format for message layout: sections, context and buttons.
The name of a button's action; app.action matches on it.
A Slack message's ID, a timestamp string; with the channel it lets you edit or reply in its thread.

tickets.why: The Bolt app in Socket Mode, /nova start, status and stop, and one status message per ticket edited with chat.update.
Every button and thread reply becomes a signal that records who did it; buttons disappear after a decision.
The plan message's Block Kit buttons carry nova:RH-1234|v2, and only the requester's click counts.
/nova maps the Slack user to a Jira accountId through config/people.yaml and hands the ticket over in Jira.

remember: ack() within 3 seconds, then turn each command, click and reply into a Temporal call that records who did it.
